title: Big To-Do's band and Saturday parties in Mississippi
summary: He played drums with Big To-Do's five-piece and at weekend parties with gambling behind a sheet while the show owner was away.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So I had two little bottles of senso(?), you know, for ...(?)... He must have never seen them; he took those. He just took them. Then a wagon came and trucked all of my stuff. Because I had the drum set; you know, I was playing the drums. I got to the job right quick! I was with ...(?)..., we were cracking up last night, because the guy who had the band was so big he got called Big To-Do.

Big To-Do. Heh-heh, heh-heh-heh. That was his name. We had five pieces, have a girl playing piano... I don't remember none of those cats. I remember his name. We used to travel in his car and play over in Mississippi. We used to play a place, I forget what the hell the name of
the town is, in Mississippi on... We'd go there Saturday, Saturday night.

See, Captain John would go away; he would be away for the weekend, you know. So they would party from Saturday night to Sunday night, then they had to be straight with the house clean for Monday, you know. At least their part of the house, where they... They had like a big room, like this, but they had this sheet down on one side for the dancing and refreshments, and the other side was for gambling. So we was over there with a few of us playing the music, you know. So every once in a while, they'd ...(?). They'd hear that Captain John was on his way back, so then everybody's got to split! -- heh-heh.
That was... You see, you got all you wanted to drink and all to eat, you know. Maybe two bottles, maybe three.
No! With a sheet up there, it's legal...?! Wasn't no Vegas then.
